data.summary: Antihistamines · First-generation H1 antihistamine — piperidine; also serotonin (5-HT2) antagonist
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** First-generation H1 antihistamine — piperidine; also serotonin (5-HT2) antagonist

## Mechanism of action
- Blocks H1 and 5-HT2 receptors; anticholinergic; appetite stimulant

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Cold urticaria (drug of choice among older agents), chronic urticaria, pruritus
- Serotonin syndrome (antidote), appetite stimulation, migraine prophylaxis in children

## Dose & formulations
- 4 mg three times daily (max 32 mg/day); children 0.25 mg/kg/day

## Adverse effects
- Sedation, increased appetite and weight gain, anticholinergic effects

## Contraindications
- Glaucoma, urinary retention, neonates, elderly debilitated

## Drug interactions
- Reduces effect of SSRIs; CNS depressants

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid in late pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Antiserotonergic — cold urticaria and serotonin syndrome; causes weight gain

_Sources: Khopkar (First generation H1 antihistamines); Wolverton 4e ch.32. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
